records.source: וְאִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נִשְׁבַּ֥ע בַּמִּצְפָּ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר אִ֣ישׁ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ לֹא־יִתֵּ֥ן בִּתּ֛וֹ לְבִנְיָמִ֖ן לְאִשָּֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And [the] man of Israel had sworn at Mizpah, saying, a man of us not will give his daughter to Benjamin for a wife.
pieces: Now the men of Israel had taken an oath at Mizpah: "None of us will give his daughter in marriage to a man of Benjamin."

L.1: And the men of Israel had sworn at Mizpah, saying, "Not one of us shall give his daughter to Benjamin as a wife."

R.1: Earlier, at Mizpah, the men of Israel had made a promise with an oath. They had said, "None of us will let his daughter marry a man from the tribe of Benjamin."

decisions.choice: had sworn: an oath made earlier, at the gathering in Mizpah
decisions.reason: The verb looks back. Chapter 20 tells of the gathering at Mizpah (20:1-11) but does not report this oath; it is told now because the story turns on it. Everything in this chapter is an attempt to keep the oath and still save the tribe.

decisions.choice: the man of Israel: the men of Israel together, the fighting men of the assembly
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the singular "man" for the whole body of Israelite men, as in 20:11 ("all the men of Israel ... as one man"). Those who swore are the fathers who could give daughters in marriage.

decisions.choice: give his daughter to Benjamin as a wife: refuse all marriage with the tribe
decisions.reason: Fathers arranged their daughters' marriages, so the oath shut Benjamin out of marriage with every other tribe. With Benjamin's own women killed (20:48; 21:16), the oath meant the tribe would die out.

decisions.choice: to a man of Benjamin / to a man from the tribe of Benjamin
decisions.reason: "Benjamin" here is the tribe, and in practice its surviving men; Balanced and Readable say so. Readable also adds "Earlier" to show the oath came before the events just told.

records.heading: The tribes grieve for Benjamin

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֤א הָעָם֙ בֵּֽית־אֵ֔ל וַיֵּ֤שְׁבוּ שָׁם֙ עַד־הָעֶ֔רֶב לִפְנֵ֖י הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיִּשְׂא֣וּ קוֹלָ֔ם וַיִּבְכּ֖וּ בְּכִ֥י גָדֽוֹל׃
records.gloss: And came the people [to] Bethel, and they sat there until the evening before the God, and they lifted up their voice and they wept [a] great weeping.
pieces: The people went to Bethel and sat there before God until evening, weeping aloud and bitterly.

L.2: And the people came to Bethel and sat there until evening before God, and they lifted up their voices and wept with great weeping.

R.2: The people went to Bethel. They sat there in front of God until evening, crying loudly and bitterly.

decisions.choice: Bethel, before God: at the place where the ark of the covenant then stood
decisions.reason: In this war the Israelites went up to Bethel to ask God for guidance, because the ark was there with Phinehas the priest (20:18, 26-28). To sit "before God" is to be at his sanctuary, in his presence.

decisions.choice: lifted up their voices and wept with great weeping: loud, bitter mourning
decisions.reason: Raising the voice and weeping is the sign of deep grief (2:4; 20:23, 26). Here the people mourn the loss of a tribe, though it was their own army that destroyed it (20:48).

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ לָמָ֗ה יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הָ֥יְתָה זֹּ֖את בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לְהִפָּקֵ֥ד הַיּ֛וֹם מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שֵׁ֥בֶט אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: And they said, why, YHWH God of Israel, has happened this in Israel, to be missing today from Israel tribe one?
pieces: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Israel," they cried, "why has this happened in Israel? Why should Israel be missing one of its tribes today?"

L.3: And they said, "Why, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Israel, has this happened in Israel, that today one tribe should be missing from Israel?"

R.3: They prayed, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Israel, why has this happened in Israel? Why is one tribe missing from Israel today?"

decisions.choice: Why has this happened? A lament that brings the loss before God
decisions.reason: The question is a cry of grief, not a request for information. The answer is plain from the story: Benjamin protected the men of Gibeah (20:13), and Israel's army destroyed the tribe's towns and people (20:48) and swore the oath of verse 1. The people speak as if the disaster had simply come on them.

decisions.choice: be missing: be counted and found lacking
decisions.reason: The verb belongs to the language of counting. When Israel is counted, one tribe will be absent. The same root is used for the muster in verse 9.

decisions.choice: prayed
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "they said". The words are addressed to God, so Readable says they prayed.

records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ הָעָ֔ם וַיִּבְנוּ־שָׁ֖ם מִזְבֵּ֑חַ וַיַּעֲל֥וּ עֹל֖וֹת וּשְׁלָמִֽים׃פ
records.gloss: And it was on the next day, and rose early the people, and they built there an altar, and they offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings.
pieces: Early the next morning the people built an altar there and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings.

L.4: And it happened on the next day that the people rose early and built an altar there, and they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings.

R.4: Early the next morning the people built an altar there. They offered burnt offerings and peace offerings.

decisions.choice: built an altar there: a new altar at Bethel for this occasion
decisions.reason: Israel had already offered sacrifices at Bethel during the war (20:26). Why a new altar was needed is not said; the narrator records only that the people built one before seeking a way out of their oath.

decisions.choice: burnt offerings and peace offerings: seeking God's favor in a time of crisis
decisions.reason: A burnt offering was burned whole for the LORD (Leviticus 1); a peace offering was shared in a meal before him (Leviticus 3). The same pair is offered at Bethel in 20:26, after the second defeat, and by Saul before battle in 1 Samuel 13:9.

records.source: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִ֠י אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹא־עָלָ֧ה בַקָּהָ֛ל מִכָּל־שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל־יְהוָ֑ה כִּי֩ הַשְּׁבוּעָ֨ה הַגְּדוֹלָ֜ה הָיְתָ֗ה לַ֠אֲשֶׁר לֹא־עָלָ֨ה אֶל־יְהוָ֧ה הַמִּצְפָּ֛ה לֵאמֹ֖ר מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃
records.gloss: And said [the] sons of Israel, who [is there] who not went up in the assembly from all [the] tribes of Israel to YHWH? For the oath the great had been concerning whoever not went up to YHWH [to] the Mizpah, saying, surely he shall be put to death.
pieces: Then the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} asked, "Is there anyone from all the tribes of Israel who did not come up with the assembly to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?" For they had bound themselves by a solemn oath: whoever stayed away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at Mizpah must be put to death.

L.5: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel said, "Who [is there] among all the tribes of Israel who did not come up in the assembly to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?" For the great oath had been concerning whoever did not come up to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at Mizpah, saying, "He shall surely be put to death."

R.5: Then the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} asked, "Did anyone from the tribes of Israel fail to come to the gathering before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?" They asked because they had made a serious promise with an oath: anyone who did not come to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at Mizpah would be put to death.

decisions.choice: the great oath: a second oath, made at Mizpah, against anyone who stayed away
decisions.reason: Besides the oath of verse 1, the assembly had sworn that anyone who refused the call to Mizpah (20:1) would die. A summons to the tribes in a time of war carried such a threat; compare Saul's summons in 1 Samuel 11:7. The oath is what gives the assembly a reason to attack Jabesh-gilead (verses 8-10).

decisions.choice: he shall surely be put to death: the legal formula for a death sentence
decisions.reason: The doubled verb is the form the law uses for crimes that carry the death penalty (Exodus 21:12, 15-17; Leviticus 20:2). It is emphatic: the penalty must be carried out.

decisions.choice: For the great oath had been: the narrator explains the question
decisions.reason: The question about who stayed away is not idle; the narrator adds the reason. The verb looks back to the gathering at Mizpah, like "had sworn" in verse 1.

decisions.choice: the oath reported, not quoted
alternatives: "He shall surely be put to death"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the oath's own words in quotation marks. Balanced and Readable report it in the narrator's words, which reads more easily inside an explanation; Readable also says "They asked because" for the Hebrew "for".

records.heading: Wives from Jabesh-gilead

records.source: וַיִּנָּֽחֲמוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶל־בִּנְיָמִ֖ן אָחִ֑יו וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ נִגְדַּ֥ע הַיּ֛וֹם שֵׁ֥בֶט אֶחָ֖ד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And were sorry [the] sons of Israel for Benjamin his brother, and they said, cut off today [is] one tribe from Israel.
pieces: But the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} grieved for their brother tribe Benjamin. "Today," they said, "one tribe has been cut off from Israel.

L.6: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel had compassion for Benjamin their brother, and they said, "Today one tribe has been cut off from Israel.

R.6: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} felt sorry for the tribe of Benjamin, because the people of Benjamin were their own relatives. They said, "Today one tribe has been cut off from Israel.

decisions.choice: had compassion: grieved and felt pity, enough to want to act
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to be sorry, to grieve, to be comforted, or to change one's mind. Here Israel grieves over what has happened to Benjamin, and the grief leads to the search for wives that follows. The same verb comes back in verse 15.

decisions.choice: Benjamin his brother: a brother tribe, descended from the same father
decisions.reason: The tribes were the families of Jacob's sons, and Benjamin was the youngest (Genesis 35:18). The Hebrew says "his brother", treating Israel as one person. In the war itself the Israelites had called Benjamin "my brother" (20:23, 28).

decisions.choice: cut off: hewn off, like a branch chopped from a tree
decisions.reason: The verb is used for cutting down trees and cutting off a horn or a limb. Only 600 men of Benjamin were left (20:47); the tribe is cut away from the people as a whole.

decisions.choice: because the people of Benjamin were their own relatives
decisions.reason: Readable explains "their brother": the tribes were related families.

records.source: מַה־נַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה לָהֶ֛ם לַנּוֹתָרִ֖ים לְנָשִׁ֑ים וַאֲנַ֨חְנוּ֙ נִשְׁבַּ֣עְנוּ בַֽיהוָ֔ה לְבִלְתִּ֛י תֵּת־לָהֶ֥ם מִבְּנוֹתֵ֖ינוּ לְנָשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: What shall we do for them, for the ones remaining, for wives, and we, we have sworn by YHWH not to give to them from our daughters for wives?
pieces: How can we provide wives for the men who are left, since we have sworn by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} not to give them any of our daughters in marriage?"

L.7: What shall we do for them, for those who remain, for wives, since we have sworn by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} not to give them any of our daughters as wives?"

R.7: The men who are left have no wives. How can we find wives for them? We swore by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that we would not let them marry our daughters."

decisions.choice: those who remain: the 600 men of Benjamin at the rock of Rimmon
decisions.reason: Only 600 men escaped the battle and fled to the rock of Rimmon (20:47). Israel's army had then killed everyone in Benjamin's towns (20:48), so the survivors had no wives and no women of their own tribe left (verse 16).

decisions.choice: we have sworn by the LORD: an oath that cannot simply be broken
decisions.reason: An oath made in the LORD's name bound the one who swore it (Numbers 30:3; Deuteronomy 23:22-24). The assembly's own oath now stands in the way of saving the tribe, and the rest of the chapter is spent finding ways around it.

decisions.choice: The men who are left have no wives.
alternatives: What shall we do for them ... for wives
decisions.reason: Readable states the problem first in its own sentence, then asks the question.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מִ֗י אֶחָד֙ מִשִּׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־עָלָ֥ה אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה הַמִּצְפָּ֑ה וְ֠הִנֵּה לֹ֣א בָא־אִ֧ישׁ אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֛ה מִיָּבֵ֥ישׁ גִּלְעָ֖ד אֶל־הַקָּהָֽל׃
records.gloss: And they said, who [is] one from [the] tribes of Israel which not went up to YHWH [to] the Mizpah? And behold, not had come a man to the camp from Jabesh-gilead, to the assembly.
pieces: So they asked, "Who from the tribes of Israel did not come up to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at Mizpah?" It turned out that not a single man from Jabesh-gilead had come into the camp to join the assembly.

L.8: And they said, "Which one of the tribes of Israel did not come up to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at Mizpah?" And look, no one had come to the camp from Jabesh-gilead, to the assembly.

R.8: So they asked, "Which group from the tribes of Israel did not come to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at Mizpah?" They found out that no one from the town of Jabesh-gilead had come to the camp for the gathering.

decisions.choice: Jabesh-gilead: an Israelite town in Gilead, east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Jabesh lay in Gilead, in the land of the eastern tribes. The town appears again in Saul's story: Saul, a Benjaminite, rescues it from the Ammonites, and its men later bury Saul (1 Samuel 11:1-11; 31:11-13). The link between Jabesh and Benjamin begins here.

decisions.choice: look: the word marks a discovery
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word draws attention to what is found: no one from Jabesh-gilead had answered the summons. That finding brings the oath of verse 5 into force.

decisions.choice: It turned out that / They found out that
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the Hebrew "look" signals here, a discovery. Readable adds "the town of" so the name is not taken for a tribe.

records.source: וַיִּתְפָּקֵ֖ד הָעָ֑ם וְהִנֵּ֤ה אֵֽין־שָׁם֙ אִ֔ישׁ מִיּוֹשְׁבֵ֖י יָבֵ֥שׁ גִּלְעָֽד׃
records.gloss: And was mustered the people, and behold, not there [was] a man from [the] inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead.
pieces: When the people were counted, not one of those who lived in Jabesh-gilead was there.

L.9: For the people were counted, and look, there was not a man there from the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead.

R.9: They counted the people, and no one from Jabesh-gilead was there.

decisions.choice: the people were counted: how the discovery of verse 8 was made
decisions.reason: The verse goes back over what verse 8 has just said and tells how it was found: the army was counted, as troops were mustered for war, and no one from Jabesh-gilead answered. The verb is from the same root as "be missing" in verse 3.

decisions.choice: For
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "and". Literal says "For" because the verse explains the one before it rather than adding a new event.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלְחוּ־שָׁ֣ם הָעֵדָ֗ה שְׁנֵים־עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֛לֶף אִ֖ישׁ מִבְּנֵ֣י הֶחָ֑יִל וַיְצַוּ֨וּ אוֹתָ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר לְ֠כוּ וְהִכִּיתֶ֞ם אֶת־יוֹשְׁבֵ֨י יָבֵ֤שׁ גִּלְעָד֙ לְפִי־חֶ֔רֶב וְהַנָּשִׁ֖ים וְהַטָּֽף׃
records.gloss: And sent there the congregation twelve thousand men from the sons of the strength, and they commanded them, saying, go and strike [the] inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead to [the] mouth of [the] sword, and the women and the little ones.
pieces: So the congregation sent 12,000 of its best fighting men there with these orders: "Go and put the people of Jabesh-gilead to the sword, the women and children too.

L.10: And the congregation sent 12,000 men of the valiant there and commanded them, saying, "Go and strike the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead with the edge of the sword, even the women and the little ones.

R.10: The community sent 12,000 of its best soldiers there. They gave them this order: "Go and kill everyone who lives in Jabesh-gilead, even the women and children.

decisions.choice: the sons of strength: capable, proven warriors
decisions.reason: "Sons of" a quality are people marked by it. "Strength" here is strength in battle, so these are the army's best fighting men (compare 20:44, 46).

decisions.choice: with the edge of the sword: kill in battle
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "to the mouth of the sword", the blade pictured as a mouth that devours. The phrase means to kill with the sword (1:8, 25; 20:37, 48).

decisions.choice: even the women and the little ones: the death sentence of the oath widened to a whole town
decisions.reason: The oath of verse 5 threatened death to anyone who stayed away. Now the assembly turns it against an entire Israelite town, families included, in part to find wives. The narrator reports it without praise and closes the book with the verdict of verse 25.

decisions.choice: children
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means "little ones", the young children of a household. Balanced and Readable say "children"; Literal keeps "little ones".

records.source: וְזֶ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ כָּל־זָכָ֗ר וְכָל־אִשָּׁ֛ה יֹדַ֥עַת מִשְׁכַּב־זָכָ֖ר תַּחֲרִֽימוּ׃
records.gloss: And this [is] the thing that you shall do: every male and every woman knowing [the] lying of a male you shall devote to destruction.
pieces: Here is what you must do: every male, and every woman who has slept with a man, you are to devote to destruction."

L.11: And this is the thing that you shall do: every male, and every woman who has known lying with a male, you shall devote to destruction."

R.11: This is what you must do. Destroy completely, as given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, every male and every woman who has slept with a man."

decisions.choice: devote to destruction: give over to God by destroying completely
decisions.reason: The verb belongs to the practice of devoting something or someone to God so that it is destroyed and no one keeps it (Joshua 6:17-21). The law used it for an Israelite town that turned to other gods (Deuteronomy 13:13-19). Here it is turned against an Israelite town whose offense was staying away from the assembly, and it is not complete: the young women are spared to be wives (verse 12).

decisions.choice: every male and every woman who has known a man: the words of the war on Midian
decisions.reason: Moses ordered the army to kill every male among the children of Midian and every woman who had known a man, and to keep alive the girls who had not (Numbers 31:17-18). The assembly takes that command against foreign enemies and applies it to fellow Israelites.

decisions.choice: known the lying of a male: had sexual relations with a man
decisions.reason: "Know" is the usual Hebrew way of speaking of sexual relations (Genesis 4:1), and "the lying of a male" makes the meaning plain. The women spared are the virgins, as verse 12 says.

decisions.choice: Destroy completely, as given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable explains the verb, as the Numbers-to-Ruth wording does everywhere: destruction that hands the people over to God. The LORD is not named in this verse; Readable names him because that is what the verb means.

records.source: וַֽיִּמְצְא֞וּ מִיּוֹשְׁבֵ֣י׀יָבֵ֣ישׁ גִּלְעָ֗ד אַרְבַּ֤ע מֵאוֹת֙ נַעֲרָ֣ה בְתוּלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹֽא־יָדְעָ֛ה אִ֖ישׁ לְמִשְׁכַּ֣ב זָכָ֑ר וַיָּבִ֨יאוּ אוֹתָ֤ם אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶה֙ שִׁלֹ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּאֶ֥רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן׃ס
records.gloss: And they found from [the] inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead four hundred young women, virgins, who not had known a man by lying of a male, and they brought them to the camp [at] Shiloh, which [is] in [the] land of Canaan.
pieces: Among the people of Jabesh-gilead they found 400 young women who were virgins and had never slept with a man. These they brought to the camp at Shiloh, in the land of Canaan.

L.12: And they found among the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead 400 young women, virgins, who had not known a man by lying with a male; and they brought them to the camp at Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan.

R.12: Among the people of Jabesh-gilead they found 400 young women who had never slept with a man. They took them to the Israelite camp at Shiloh, in the land of Canaan.

decisions.choice: the camp at Shiloh, in the land of Canaan: the sanctuary town west of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The tent of meeting had been set up at Shiloh (Joshua 18:1), and it was still there in Samuel's youth (1 Samuel 1:3). "In the land of Canaan" sets Shiloh apart from Gilead, east of the Jordan (compare Joshua 22:9). The narrator does not say why the camp is now at Shiloh rather than Bethel.

decisions.choice: young women, virgins: unmarried girls of marriageable age
decisions.reason: The first word means a girl or young woman; the second an unmarried young woman. The clause that follows defines it: they had never had relations with a man. They are spared because they can become wives for Benjamin.

decisions.choice: who had never slept with a man
alternatives: virgins who had never slept with a man
decisions.reason: Readable keeps one plain description for the two Hebrew expressions that say the same thing.

records.source: וַֽיִּשְׁלְחוּ֙ כָּל־הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה וַֽיְדַבְּרוּ֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּסֶ֣לַע רִמּ֑וֹן וַיִּקְרְא֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם שָׁלֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And sent all the congregation, and they spoke to [the] sons of Benjamin who [were] at [the] rock of Rimmon, and they proclaimed to them peace.
pieces: Then the whole congregation sent word to the Benjaminites at the rock of Rimmon and offered them peace.

L.13: And the whole congregation sent and spoke to the sons of Benjamin who were at the rock of Rimmon, and proclaimed peace to them.

R.13: Then the whole community sent a message to the men of Benjamin at the rock of Rimmon, offering to make peace with them.

decisions.choice: the rock of Rimmon: the wilderness refuge of the 600 survivors
decisions.reason: After the defeat, 600 men of Benjamin fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon and stayed there four months (20:45-47).

decisions.choice: proclaimed peace to them: declared the war over and offered terms
decisions.reason: To "call out peace" is to offer peace to an enemy (Deuteronomy 20:10). The tribes now treat Benjamin as a brother again rather than an enemy.

decisions.choice: the Benjaminites / the men of Benjamin
decisions.reason: The "sons of Benjamin" here are the 600 surviving men, so Balanced and Readable use a term for them; no gender setting is needed, since only men are meant.

records.source: וַיָּ֤שָׁב בִּנְיָמִן֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא וַיִּתְּנ֤וּ לָהֶם֙ הַנָּשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר חִיּ֔וּ מִנְּשֵׁ֖י יָבֵ֣שׁ גִּלְעָ֑ד וְלֹֽא־מָצְא֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם כֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: And returned Benjamin at the time the that, and they gave to them the women whom they had kept alive from [the] women of Jabesh-gilead, and not they found for them so.
pieces: So Benjamin came back at that time, and they were given the women of Jabesh-gilead whom the Israelites had spared. But there were not enough for them all.

L.14: And Benjamin returned at that time, and they gave them the women whom they had kept alive from the women of Jabesh-gilead; but even so they did not find [enough] for them.

R.14: So the men of Benjamin came back, and the Israelites gave them the women from Jabesh-gilead whom they had let live. But there were not enough women for all of them.

decisions.choice: they did not find for them so: there were not enough
decisions.reason: The words are compressed: "they did not find for them thus". The sense is that this way did not provide enough wives: 400 women (verse 12) for 600 men (20:47). That shortfall leads to the plan of verses 19-22.

decisions.choice: Benjamin returned: the survivors came back from their refuge
decisions.reason: The tribe is named in the singular for its men. They return from the rock of Rimmon (verse 13), to the other tribes and to their own land.

decisions.choice: whom the Israelites had spared / the Israelites gave them
alternatives: they gave them ... whom they had kept alive
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "they". Balanced and Readable name the Israelites so that it is clear who gave the women and who received them.

records.source: וְהָעָ֥ם נִחָ֖ם לְבִנְיָמִ֑ן כִּֽי־עָשָׂ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה פֶּ֖רֶץ בְּשִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And the people had compassion for Benjamin, for had made YHWH a breach in [the] tribes of Israel.
pieces: The people grieved for Benjamin, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had torn a gap in the tribes of Israel.

L.15: And the people had compassion for Benjamin, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had made a breach in the tribes of Israel.

R.15: The people felt sorry for the tribe of Benjamin, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had left a gap among the tribes of Israel.

decisions.choice: the LORD had made a breach: the people see God's hand in Benjamin's defeat
decisions.reason: The narrator had said that the LORD struck Benjamin before Israel (20:35). The breach is still the result of human choices as well: Benjamin's defense of Gibeah, the army's slaughter, and the oath. The verse holds both together.

decisions.choice: breach: a break, as in a wall, where something is missing
decisions.reason: The word is used for a gap broken in a city wall (1 Kings 11:27) and for the LORD's breaking out against Uzzah (2 Samuel 6:8). Here the gap is a missing tribe among the twelve.

decisions.choice: had compassion: the same feeling as in verse 6
decisions.reason: The verse takes up verse 6 again and marks a new start: the 400 women were not enough, and the people's grief drives a second plan.

records.source: וַיֹּֽאמְר֨וּ זִקְנֵ֣י הָעֵדָ֔ה מַה־נַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה לַנּוֹתָרִ֖ים לְנָשִׁ֑ים כִּֽי־נִשְׁמְדָ֥ה מִבִּנְיָמִ֖ן אִשָּֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And said [the] elders of the congregation, what shall we do for the ones remaining for wives, for destroyed from Benjamin [is the] woman?
pieces: Then the elders of the congregation said, "How can we provide wives for the men who are left, since the women of Benjamin have been wiped out?"

L.16: And the elders of the congregation said, "What shall we do for those who remain, for wives, since the women of Benjamin have been destroyed?"

R.16: The elders of the community asked, "How can we find wives for the men who are left? All the women of Benjamin have been killed."

decisions.choice: the women have been destroyed from Benjamin: killed when the towns were struck
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "woman" in the singular, meaning women as a whole. Israel's army killed everyone found in Benjamin's towns, people and animals, and burned the towns (20:48).

decisions.choice: the elders of the congregation: the heads of families who led the assembly
decisions.reason: The elders were the senior men who spoke and decided for the people (Exodus 3:16; Judges 11:5). The question repeats verse 7, now from the leaders, and leads to their plan.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ יְרֻשַּׁ֥ת פְּלֵיטָ֖ה לְבִנְיָמִ֑ן וְלֹֽא־יִמָּחֶ֥ה שֵׁ֖בֶט מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And they said, possession of [a] remnant [is] to Benjamin, and not will be wiped out a tribe from Israel.
pieces: They said, "The survivors of Benjamin must have heirs to keep their inheritance, so that a tribe is not wiped out of Israel.

L.17: And they said, "[There must be] an inheritance for the survivors of Benjamin, so that a tribe will not be wiped out from Israel.

R.17: They said, "The men of Benjamin who are still alive must have children to keep their land. Then no tribe will disappear from Israel.

decisions.choice: an inheritance for the survivors: the remnant of Benjamin must keep its land through heirs
alternatives: "How can there be an inheritance for the survivors of Benjamin?"
"The land of Benjamin belongs to its survivors"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is brief: "a possession of escaped ones for Benjamin". The likely sense is that the tribe's land must stay with its survivors and pass to their children, so that Benjamin goes on as a tribe. It may also be a question, "How can the survivors keep an inheritance?", or a statement that the land still belongs to them. The wording is hard, and the sense here follows what the elders go on to plan.

decisions.choice: wiped out from Israel: erased like a name from a record
decisions.reason: The verb means to wipe clean or blot out. A family line was said to be blotted out when no heir carried on its name (Deuteronomy 25:6). Here a whole tribe is in danger of it.

decisions.choice: must have heirs to keep their inheritance / must have children to keep their land
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the sense of the short phrase explicit, following meaning decision m1. Another reading is possible (see m1).

records.source: וַאֲנַ֗חְנוּ לֹ֥א נוּכַ֛ל לָתֵת־לָהֶ֥ם נָשִׁ֖ים מִבְּנוֹתֵ֑ינוּ כִּֽי־נִשְׁבְּע֤וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אָר֕וּר נֹתֵ֥ן אִשָּׁ֖ה לְבִנְיָמִֽן׃ס
records.gloss: And we, not we are able to give to them wives from our daughters, for had sworn [the] sons of Israel, saying, cursed [be the one] giving a wife to Benjamin.
pieces: Yet we cannot give them our daughters as wives, because the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} have sworn, 'A curse on anyone who gives a wife to Benjamin!'"

L.18: But as for us, we cannot give them wives from our daughters, for the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel have sworn, saying, 'Cursed [is the one] who gives a wife to Benjamin.'"

R.18: But we cannot let them marry our daughters. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} have made a promise with an oath: 'Anyone who gives a wife to a man from Benjamin will be cursed!'"

decisions.choice: Cursed is the one who gives: an oath backed by a curse
decisions.reason: The oath of verse 1 called down a curse on anyone who broke it, as Saul's oath did on anyone who ate during the battle (1 Samuel 14:24, 28). To give a daughter to a Benjaminite would bring the curse on the father.

decisions.choice: the reason clause is part of the elders' speech
alternatives: the narrator's comment: "For the Israelites had sworn ..."
decisions.reason: The elders speak of the oath in the third person, "the Israelites have sworn", which could also be the narrator's comment. It is read here as their own words, since it explains why "we cannot". The Hebrew has no quotation marks.

decisions.choice: to a man from Benjamin
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, Readable says what "Benjamin" means here: a man of the tribe.

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֡וּ הִנֵּה֩ חַג־יְהוָ֨ה בְּשִׁל֜וֹ מִיָּמִ֣ים׀יָמִ֗ימָה אֲשֶׁ֞ר מִצְּפ֤וֹנָה לְבֵֽית־אֵל֙ מִזְרְחָ֣ה הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ לִמְסִלָּ֔ה הָעֹלָ֥ה מִבֵּֽית־אֵ֖ל שְׁכֶ֑מָה וּמִנֶּ֖גֶב לִלְבוֹנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And they said, behold, [the] festival of YHWH [is] in Shiloh from days to days, which [is] from north to Bethel, toward [the] rising of the sun to [the] highway the going up from Bethel to Shechem, and from [the] south to Lebonah.
pieces: Then they said, "Look, every year there is a festival of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at Shiloh." (Shiloh lies north of Bethel and south of Lebonah, east of the highway that runs up from Bethel to Shechem.)

L.19: And they said, "Look, [there is] the festival of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Shiloh from year to year." ([Shiloh is] north of Bethel, toward the sunrise from the highway that goes up from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah.)

R.19: Then they said, "Every year there is a festival for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at Shiloh." (Shiloh is north of the town of Bethel and south of Lebonah. It is east of the main road from Bethel to Shechem.)

decisions.choice: the festival of the LORD: a yearly feast, perhaps at the grape harvest
alternatives: a local yearly festival at Shiloh
decisions.reason: Which festival is meant is not said. The vineyards and the dancing (verses 20-21) suggest the harvest of grapes, which fits the Festival of Booths in autumn (Leviticus 23:34-43; Deuteronomy 16:13-15). It may also be a local yearly feast at Shiloh like the one Elkanah attended (1 Samuel 1:3).

decisions.choice: from days to days: every year
decisions.reason: "From days to days" is a set phrase for a yearly event (1 Samuel 1:3; 2:19).

decisions.choice: the directions to Shiloh are the narrator's note
decisions.reason: The elders and the Benjaminites would have known where Shiloh was. The precise directions read like a note for later readers who did not, so they are set outside the quotation. The Hebrew has no quotation marks, and they could also be part of the elders' words.

decisions.choice: parentheses, and "Shiloh" named again
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the directions with "which". Setting them in parentheses and naming Shiloh shows that the narrator is speaking, following m3.

records.heading: The dance at Shiloh

records.source: וַיְצַוּ֕וּאֶת־בְּנֵ֥י בִנְיָמִ֖ן לֵאמֹ֑ר לְכ֖וּ וַאֲרַבְתֶּ֥ם בַּכְּרָמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And they commanded [the] sons of Benjamin, saying, go and you shall lie in wait in the vineyards,
pieces: So they instructed the Benjaminites, "Go and hide in the vineyards and wait,

L.20: And they commanded the sons of Benjamin, saying, "Go and lie in wait in the vineyards,

R.20: So they told the men of Benjamin, "Go and hide in the vineyards.

decisions.choice: they commanded: the plural the Hebrew text tells readers to read
decisions.reason: The written letters of the Hebrew text give "he commanded", while the marginal reading of the Masoretes, which the vowels follow, gives "they commanded". The plural fits the elders who speak in verses 16-19. The meaning of the verse is the same either way.

decisions.choice: lie in wait: set an ambush
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for an ambush in war, as in the attack on Gibeah (20:29, 33, 36-38). The Benjaminites are told to hide and wait for their moment.

decisions.choice: the Benjaminites / the men of Benjamin
decisions.reason: As in verse 13: only the surviving men are meant.

records.source: וּרְאִיתֶ֗ם וְ֠הִנֵּה אִם־יֵ֨צְא֥וּ בְנוֹת־שִׁילוֹ֮ לָח֣וּל בַּמְּחֹלוֹת֒ וִֽיצָאתֶם֙ מִן־הַכְּרָמִ֔ים וַחֲטַפְתֶּ֥ם לָכֶ֛ם אִ֥ישׁ אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ מִבְּנ֣וֹת שִׁיל֑וֹ וַהֲלַכְתֶּ֖ם אֶ֥רֶץ בִּנְיָמִֽן׃
records.gloss: and you shall watch, and behold, if come out [the] daughters of Shiloh to dance in the dances, then you shall come out from the vineyards and you shall seize for yourselves each his wife from [the] daughters of Shiloh, and you shall go [to the] land of Benjamin.
pieces: and watch. When the young women of Shiloh come out to join in the dances, rush out of the vineyards, and each of you seize a wife for himself from the young women of Shiloh. Then go back to the land of Benjamin.

L.21: and watch; and look, when the daughters of Shiloh come out to dance in the dances, then come out of the vineyards and seize for yourselves each man his wife from the daughters of Shiloh, and go to the land of Benjamin.

R.21: Watch for the young women of Shiloh to come out and dance. Then run out of the vineyards. Each of you must grab one of the young women of Shiloh to be his wife, and take her home to the land of Benjamin.

decisions.choice: to dance in the dances: women's dancing at a festival
decisions.reason: Women danced at times of celebration, with music and singing (Exodus 15:20; Judges 11:34; 1 Samuel 18:6). At the festival the young women of Shiloh would come out into the open, away from their homes.

decisions.choice: seize: snatch, carry off by force
decisions.reason: The verb is used for a robber or a lion catching its prey (Psalm 10:9). The young women are not asked; they are carried off. Verse 23 calls it "robbing".

decisions.choice: young women of Shiloh
decisions.reason: "The daughters of" a town are its girls and young women. Balanced and Readable say so; Literal keeps "daughters".

records.source: וְהָיָ֡ה כִּֽי־יָבֹ֣אוּ אֲבוֹתָם֩ א֨וֹ אֲחֵיהֶ֜ם לָרִ֣יב׀אֵלֵ֗ינוּ וְאָמַ֤רְנוּ אֲלֵיהֶם֙ חָנּ֣וּנוּ אוֹתָ֔ם כִּ֣י לֹ֥א לָקַ֛חְנוּ אִ֥ישׁ אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֑ה כִּ֣י לֹ֥א אַתֶּ֛ם נְתַתֶּ֥ם לָהֶ֖ם כָּעֵ֥ת תֶּאְשָֽׁמוּ׃ס
records.gloss: And it will be, when come their fathers or their brothers to complain to us, then we will say to them, be gracious to us [with] them, for not we took each his wife in the battle; for not you, you gave to them; at [the] time you would be guilty.
pieces: When their fathers or brothers come to us to protest, we will tell them, 'Do us a kindness and let them keep the women, because we did not take a wife for each of them in the war. And since you did not give them your daughters, you are not guilty of breaking the oath.'"

L.22: And it will be, when their fathers or their brothers come to complain to us, that we will say to them, 'Grant them to us graciously, because we did not take a wife for each man in the battle; for you did not give [them] to them, [else] now you would be guilty.'"

R.22: If their fathers or brothers come to us to complain, we will say to them, 'Please be kind to us and let the men of Benjamin keep them. When we fought against Jabesh-gilead, we did not get enough wives for all of them. And you did not give your daughters to them, so you have not broken your oath.'"

decisions.choice: to complain: the word the Hebrew text tells readers to read
decisions.reason: The written letters give a different vowel pattern, which could be read as "to be many"; the marginal reading of the Masoretes, which the vowels follow, gives "to bring a complaint". Only the second makes sense here.

decisions.choice: be gracious to us with them: do us the favor of letting them be
decisions.reason: The elders ask the families to show them kindness for the young women's sake, that is, to let the marriages stand and not demand the women back.

decisions.choice: we did not take a wife for each man in the battle: the war on Jabesh-gilead did not supply enough wives
alternatives: the Benjaminites did not take them as captives of war
decisions.reason: The elders explain that the battle against Jabesh-gilead gave only 400 women for 600 men (verses 12, 14). Another reading takes "we" as speaking for the Benjaminites: they did not capture these women as spoil of war, so the matter is not one of enemies. The first fits the story of this chapter more closely.

decisions.choice: you did not give them; otherwise you would now be guilty
alternatives: "you did not give them at the time, when you would have been guilty"
decisions.reason: The families gave nothing; their daughters were taken. So they have not broken the oath of verse 1 and are not under its curse (verse 18). Had they given their daughters, they would be guilty. The plan keeps the words of the oath while the fathers lose their daughters without consent.

decisions.choice: you are not guilty of breaking the oath / you have not broken your oath
alternatives: or now you would be guilty
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what guilt is meant, following meaning decision m4, and put the clause in a positive form.

decisions.choice: When we fought against Jabesh-gilead
decisions.reason: Readable names the battle meant, following meaning decision m3. It depends on that reading.

records.source: וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־כֵן֙ בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֔ן וַיִּשְׂא֤וּ נָשִׁים֙ לְמִסְפָּרָ֔ם מִן־הַמְּחֹלְל֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר גָּזָ֑לוּ וַיֵּלְכ֗וּ וַיָּשׁ֨וּבוּ֙ אֶל־נַ֣חֲלָתָ֔ם וַיִּבְנוּ֙ אֶת־הֶ֣עָרִ֔ים וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ בָּהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And did so [the] sons of Benjamin, and they carried off wives according to their number from the dancing women whom they seized, and they went and they returned to their inheritance, and they rebuilt the cities, and they lived in them.
pieces: The Benjaminites did just that. They carried off as many wives as there were men, from the dancers they had seized, and went back to their own land. They rebuilt their towns and settled in them.

L.23: And the sons of Benjamin did so, and carried off wives according to their number from the dancers whom they had seized; and they went and returned to their inheritance, and rebuilt the cities and lived in them.

R.23: The men of Benjamin did what the elders said. Each man caught one of the young women who were dancing and took her as his wife. Then they went back to their own land. They rebuilt their towns and lived in them.

decisions.choice: seized: robbed, took by force
decisions.reason: The verb means to rob or tear away what belongs to another (Genesis 31:31; Micah 2:2). The narrator's word shows what the plan really was.

decisions.choice: according to their number: one wife for each man still without one
decisions.reason: The 400 from Jabesh-gilead had left 200 men without wives (verse 14); each of these took one of the dancers.

decisions.choice: their inheritance, the cities: Benjamin's allotted land and the towns burned in the war
decisions.reason: The inheritance is the land given to the tribe (Joshua 18:11-28). The towns had been burned by Israel's army (20:48); now they are rebuilt and the tribe lives on.

decisions.choice: their own land
decisions.reason: "Inheritance" here is the tribe's allotted land, so Balanced and Readable say "land". Readable also names the elders as the ones whose plan was carried out.

records.source: וַיִּתְהַלְּכ֨וּ מִשָּׁ֤ם בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא אִ֥ישׁ לְשִׁבְט֖וֹ וּלְמִשְׁפַּחְתּ֑וֹ וַיֵּצְא֣וּ מִשָּׁ֔ם אִ֖ישׁ לְנַחֲלָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And dispersed from there [the] sons of Israel at the time the that, each to his tribe and to his clan, and they went out from there each to his inheritance.
pieces: At that time the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} left that place and went home, each man to his own tribe and clan, each to his own land.

L.24: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel went away from there at that time, each man to his tribe and to his clan; and they went out from there, each to his inheritance.

R.24: Then the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} left there. Each man went home to his own tribe and family, to the land that belonged to him.

decisions.choice: each to his inheritance: the people go home, as at the end of Joshua
decisions.reason: Joshua's work ended with the people sent away, each to his inheritance (Joshua 24:28; Judges 2:6). Judges closes its own story with the same picture, but after a civil war rather than a covenant.

decisions.choice: his tribe and his clan: the larger and smaller units of Israel
decisions.reason: Each tribe was made up of clans, groups of related families (Joshua 7:14). The men return to their own people and land.

decisions.choice: each man
decisions.reason: Those who go home are the men of the assembly and the army (20:2, 17), so "man" and "his" are kept with no gender setting.

records.source: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם אֵ֥ין מֶ֖לֶךְ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אִ֛ישׁ הַיָּשָׁ֥ר בְּעֵינָ֖יו יַעֲשֶֽׂה׃
records.gloss: In the days the those there [was] no king in Israel; each the right in his eyes he did.
pieces: In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what they thought was right.

L.25: In those days [there was] no king in Israel; each did what [was] right in his own eyes.

R.25: At that time Israel had no king. Everyone did whatever seemed right to them.

decisions.choice: each did what was right in his own eyes: each person was his own standard
decisions.reason: As in 17:6. Israel was to do "what is right in the eyes of the LORD" (Deuteronomy 12:25, 28; 13:19), and Moses warned against each one doing "whatever is right in his own eyes" (Deuteronomy 12:8). This chapter shows it: oaths sworn in anger, an Israelite town destroyed, and young women carried off, all to keep the words of a vow.

decisions.choice: there was no king in Israel: the refrain that closes the book
decisions.reason: The saying first appears in full at 17:6, its first half in 18:1 and 19:1, and now it is the book's last sentence. It looks back from a time when Israel had kings and sums up the disorder of chapters 17-21. The book does not say whether a human king would solve the problem; Gideon had said that the LORD was Israel's ruler (8:23), and the request for a king in 1 Samuel 8 is told as a rejection of God's rule.

decisions.choice: everyone did what they thought was right
decisions.reason: As in 17:6: "in his own eyes" means by one's own judgment, and the saying covers all the people, so Balanced and Readable say "everyone ... they". Literal keeps the Hebrew picture.
